clue.text: Capital chap to follow in the morning

indicators.note: the man comes after the morning abbreviation, so these words order the two pieces

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for ante meridiem, the morning hours
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A fellow is told to tail someone first thing in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Amman is the capital city of Jordan.

clue.text: Positions assumed by a duettist

indicators.note: the letters take on a new form, as a pose is assumed, so the fodder words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer in a duet strikes various poses on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Attitudes in ballet and art are bodily postures or stances.

clue.text: Bird turning a sheep about endlessly

indicators.note: turning round makes the words a sheep read from the back

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

indicators.note: without its end, the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a bout is a spell or turn, as in a bout of illness, matching about in the sense of around

explanation.surface: A bird circles a sheep over and over without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses A RAM to make MARA; 'endlessly' trims BOUT (a round or spell) to BOU.
explanation.definitionFit: The marabou is a large African stork.

clue.text: Ones differing from 25

parts.note: 25 down is the votes in favour, so those that differ are the votes against

explanation.surface: Some people disagree with the answer at 25.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes against are the opposite of votes in favour in a division.

clue.text: Killer craft

explanation.definitionFit: A wrecker or killer of things, and also a type of small fast warship.

clue.text: Musical scholar expected to succeed

parts.note: a scholar is one who studies
a prince is the heir expected to succeed to the throne

explanation.surface: A bright pupil is tipped to win and follow on to greater things.
explanation.definitionFit: The Student Prince is a 1924 operetta by Sigmund Romberg, a stage show with songs.

clue.text: Gamble taken by knight rising against the king

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A chess player takes a chance moving a knight up against the opposing king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SIR into RIS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To gamble is to take a chance or hazard.

clue.text: Born not so long ago

parts.note: someone born more recently than another is the lesser in age

explanation.definitionFit: Being of fewer years means having been born more recently.

clue.text: One backing a horse, it may be added

definitions.meaning: one sitting on a horse's back
a clause added to a contract or bill

explanation.definitionFit: A horseman sits on a horse's back, and an extra clause appended to a document is also called this.

clue.text: Bombastic and pressing after the start

indicators.note: the pressing word comes after that opening letter
the start of the word the is its first letter

parts.note: pressing means urgent

explanation.surface: Someone is blustering and insistent from the very outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the start' gives T; 'after' puts URGENT behind it. The word is an old one for swollen or inflated in style.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word means swelling, and so inflated or pompous in language.

clue.text: Something even Old Moore couldn't visualise?

definitions.text: Something even Old Moore couldn't visualise?

parts.words: Something even Old Moore couldn't visualise?
parts.note: Old Moore's Almanack is a British yearly book of predictions, so what it could not foresee is the unpredicted

explanation.walkthrough: Old Moore's Almanack is a long-running British almanac of astrological forecasts.
explanation.definitionFit: What a prophet cannot predict is by nature unexpected or unpredicted.

clue.text: Lake Success channel not safe?

parts.note: Lake Success, New York, was the temporary headquarters of the United Nations
a sound is a sea channel or strait

explanation.surface: A stretch of water at a New York lake looks dangerous to cross.
explanation.walkthrough: The United Nations met at Lake Success, New York, from 1946 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unreliable or insecure is not sound, hence not safe.

clue.text: The updated bombardon as initially heard

definitions.text: The updated bombardon as initially heard

parts.words: The updated bombardon as initially heard
parts.note: the bombardon was an early bass brass instrument, and the modern version replaced it in the band

explanation.definitionFit: A bombardon is an old bass brass instrument, a forerunner of the large valved bass horn in bands today.

clue.text: Two ways to get round a cat-like creature

indicators.note: the get word goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
two compass directions, east and north, E and N

explanation.surface: Two routes lead around an animal resembling a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts EN (east and north, two ways or directions) inside GET.
explanation.definitionFit: The genet is a small spotted carnivore related to the civet, looking like a slender cat.

clue.text: Seaweed for a bony pike

parts.note: the gar or garpike is a long bony fish

explanation.surface: A bony fish is exchanged for some seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: This jelly comes from red seaweed and is often used loosely as a name for the weed itself.

clue.text: Relatives in a way said to be hard-up

indicators.note: the relatives word sits inside the way abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
kin means relatives

explanation.surface: Family members on a certain road are reported to be broke.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for having no money, penniless.

clue.text: Tip over in the Home Counties for vengeance

indicators.note: the turned piece goes inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE

indicators.note: turned over, so the word tip reads backwards

explanation.surface: Rubbish is dumped near London out of revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns TIP into PIT, which 'in' puts inside SE; the Home Counties are the counties around London.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite is malicious ill will, a desire for revenge.

clue.text: Proust in a tight situation?

parts.note: the second word of the answer, made drunken, is shuffled into the name of the French novelist

explanation.surface: The French novelist finds himself in a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, STUPOR made 'drunken' (an anagram signal) becomes PROUST; 'tight' means drunk, so the definition is a state of being tight.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tight is being drunk, so a state of senseless intoxication is a tight condition.

clue.text: By which, appropriately, incomes are adversely affected

definitions.text: By which, appropriately, incomes are adversely affected

parts.words: By which, appropriately, incomes are adversely affected
parts.note: money spent reduces money earned, and spending is literally the opposite of coming in

explanation.definitionFit: Expenditure, the money that goes out, eats into money that comes in.

clue.text: Napoleon's file back from Moscow, for instance

definitions.text: Napoleon's file back from Moscow, for instance

parts.words: Napoleon's file back from Moscow, for instance
parts.note: a file is a line of soldiers, and going back from Moscow was a withdrawal

explanation.definitionFit: The route an army takes when withdrawing, as Napoleon's army did from Moscow in 1812.

clue.text: Unheard of way to communicate

parts.note: unheard of means not familiar, but here a method of understanding speech without hearing it

explanation.definitionFit: Deaf people can follow speech by watching mouth movements, a method that needs no sound.

clue.text: Coastal backwater

parts.note: a backwater is usually a quiet place, but here it is water going back from the coast

explanation.definitionFit: The receding of the sea from the shore after high water is water flowing back.

clue.text: Father's Pennsylvania double

indicators.note: doubled, so the state abbreviation is written twice

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for the US state of Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: Dad has a twin living in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: An affectionate word for a dad; the 's reads as 'is'.

clue.text: National gallery discovered by a drop-out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A school dropout stumbles upon a national art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prado is Spain's national art museum in Madrid.

clue.text: Bloomer commonly 25 around the Orient

indicators.note: the slang money word goes around the eastern abbreviation

parts.note: pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
the Orient is the East, E

explanation.surface: A flower is usually given a score of twenty-five around the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' means in slang: a PONY is British slang for £25. 'around' puts it round E. 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant is something that blooms, here a showy garden flower.

clue.text: Flowing sort of robe in Spain

definitions.text: Flowing sort of robe in Spain

indicators.note: a sort of robe is the word robe in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A loose garment is worn in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a major river flowing through northern Spain.

clue.text: Up-and-down time

indicators.note: the word reads the same going up and down the grid, a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A period when things go up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is a particular time of day.

clue.text: They're all for it when it comes to the vote

definitions.text: They're all for it when it comes to the vote

parts.words: They're all for it when it comes to the vote
parts.note: those who support a motion vote in favour of it

explanation.definitionFit: Votes in favour of a motion in parliament are cast by its supporters.

clue.text: A type of measurement one takes for a plant

parts.note: a type measurement gives AN, the form of the article before the printing unit
an em is a printer's measurement of type width
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener measures out a plant one unit at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A type of measurement' gives AN EM: an em is a printer's unit. ONE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone is a flowering plant of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Delightful as any isle could be

indicators.note: the letters of any isle could be rearranged to form a new word

explanation.surface: Any island might seem blissful.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly or blissful, like the Elysian Fields of Greek myth.

clue.text: Cared in no way for an authorative decree

indicators.note: in no particular way, the letters of the fodder are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shows no interest at all in a formal ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an official order or regulation issued by authority.

clue.text: Hoodwinks a twister on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the twister goes inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: board stands for ship, SS being the steamship abbreviation
an eel twists and wriggles

explanation.surface: A tornado aboard a ship deceives everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: To seel is to stitch shut a hawk's eyes, hence to blind or hoodwink.
explanation.definitionFit: Falconers sewed shut a young hawk's eyelids, so the verb came to mean blind or deceive.
